## 1. Summary

<!--# 
With a maximum of 300 words, describe the indicator in general terms as you would to a non-expert. Think of this as a kind of common language summary. Follow the four numbers sub-headers below. under point 2, it is possible under  include a bullet point list of the specific steps in the workflow. 
 -->

1. **Background and rationale**:
Concentration of total nitrogen in the surface layer =< 10m depth during the summer and winter seasons are two of the physical-chemical support parameters for the classification of ecological status in the water masses in Norwegian coastal waters under the Water Framework Directive and the Norwegian Water Regulation. Nitrogen concentration in summer and winter are included as two separate indicators. The summer period better captures the degree of excess influx of nitrogen during the summer season (june-august), when phytoplankton growth consumes a substantial part of the nutrients in the water masses, whereas winter measurements can reveal nutrient concentrations exceeding natural background levels in a water body.


2. **Methods**:
The data are classified according to the national guidelines for classification of ecological status under the WFD (DGVF 2026).

3. **Interpretation**:
<!-- Add a very short description of how the indicator values should be interpreted. Here's an example for a bumblebee indicator: An indicator value of 1 signifies an intact bumblebee community. Values decreasing toward zero reflect negative ecological change, specifically the decline of species expected to be present. This metric does not account for potentially positive changes, such as increases in species' abundance or the arrival of new species. Tip: Add text on the line directly following the subheader, and don't introduce blank lines. This way the whole paragraph renders as a block quote. -->
An EQR value close to 1 indicates low effects of inputs and discharges. Values below 0.6 reflect nitrogen concentrations above what is considered good ecological status. 

4. **Results and development needs**:
<!-- Briefly, what does the indicator say about the ecosystem condition. What is the current status of  the metric (can it be used or is it still in development), and what immediate tasks remain to improve the indicator or to make the indicator operational -->
The current implementation uses Vannmiljø monitoring data and provides a transparent and reproducible workflow for selecting and calculating the values which are used for determining the nEQR, and determining the nEQR. Future development should focus on broader geographic coverage, automated linkage to national typology datasets and formal uncertainty estimation. Combining total nitrogen with other support parameters to form a combined indicator could be considered.

## 2. About the underlying data

<!--# Give a general introduction the datasets you have used, and provide more specific details in the sub-chapters.  -->

Data are obtained from Vannmiljø. Observations are recorded at individual monitoring stations, sampling dates and sampling depths. Determination of nEQR of total nitrogen during summer and winter is based on averaging values from 0-10 m depth from June, July and August, and from December, January and February, respectively, and from three years of observations. The current implementation selects stations with data from 2022, 2023 and 2024, and minimum 2 out of 3 months for each of the seasons.

### 2.1 Spatial and temporal resolution and extent

<!--# Describe the temporal and spatial resolution and extent of the data used -->
Measurements of total nitrogen is collected at a relatively limited number of fixed monitoring stations. For monitoring under the water framework directive measurements are made monthly. However, the nEQR is determined based on three years of observations.


### 2.2 Sampling design

<!-- How was the data sampled? Describe potential sampling biases -->


#### Field sampling and laboratory analysis  
Monitoring follows protocols developed for Norwegian coastal ecosystem monitoring and the Water Framework Directive.
Samples are taken by boat in most cases with self-closing water samplers from discrete depths, usually 10, 5 and 0 m. Water samples of 100 mL are fixed with H2SO4 in the field and analyzed according to  NS-EN ISO 15681-2  at an accredited laboratory.

Detailed descriptions of field procedures are provided in Klassifiseringsveilederen .


### 2.3 Original units

<!--# What are the original units for the most relevant  variables in the data-->

The unit is microgram nitrogen per liter "µg/l N"
### 2.4 Instructions for citing, using and accessing data

<!--# Is the data openly available? If not, how can one access it? What are the key references to the datasets?   -->

The data can be downloaded from The Environment Agency's database *Vannmiljø* at https://vannmiljo.miljodirektoratet.no/. They are licenced by Norsk lisens for offentlige data (NLOD) 2.0 (https://data.norge.no/nlod).

## 4. Reference condition and levels

### 4.1 Reference condition

<!--# Define the reference condition (or refer to where it is defined). Note the distinction between reference condition and reference levels 10.3897/oneeco.5.e58216  -->

There is no established reference condition (value) for Total Nitrogen.

### 4.2 Reference levels

<!--# 

If relevant (i.e. if you have normalised a variable), describe the reference levels used to normalise the variable. 

Use the terminology where X~0~ refers to the reference level (the variable value) denoting the worst possible condition; X~100~denotes the optimum or best possible condition; and X~*n*~, where in is between 0 and 100, denotes any other anchoring points linking the variable scale to the indicator scale (e.g. the threshold value between good and bad condition X~60^). 

Why was the current option chosen and how were the reference levels quantified? If the reference values are calculated as part of the analyses further down, please repeat the main information here.

-->
The reference levels for Total Nitrogen in Norwegian coastal waters are determined for three salinity categories: 0-5 PSU, 5-18 PSU and over 18 PSU. (klassifiseringsveilederen, xx-xx-2026)

Summer:
|Salinity | X~100~ | X~80~ | X~60~ | X~40~ | X~20~ | X~0~|
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
|<5 PSU | NA | <250	| 250-383 | 383-538 | 538-800 | >800
|5-18 PSU | NA | <250 | 250-337 | 337-505 | 505-800 | >800
|>18 PSU | NA | < 250 |	250-330 | 330-500 | 500-800 | >800
 
Winter:
|Salinity | X~100~ | X~80~ | X~60~ | X~40~ | X~20~ | X~0~|
|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|---------|
|<5 PSU  | NA |<261 |	261-385	| 385-553	| 553-800	| >800 |
|5-18 PSU| NA |<291 |	291-398	| 398-559	| 559-800	| >800 |
|>18 PSU | NA |<291 |	291-380 |	380-560	| 560-800	| >800 |



**Note terminology `X~0~`**  


#### Calculation of nEQR  

The final Ecological Quality Ratio (EQR) is calculated:



$$ nEQR = case_when(value <= `X~80~` ~ 0.9,
                           value > `X~80~` & value <= `X~60~`~ 0.7,
                           value > `X~60~` & value <= `X~40~` ~ 0.5,
                           value > `X~40~` & value <= `X~20~` ~  0.3,
                           value > `X~20~` ~ 0.1)) $$




#### 4.2.1 Spatial resolution and validity

<!--# 

Describe the spatial resolution of the reference levels. E.g. is it defined as a fixed value for all areas, or does it vary. Also, at what spatial scale are the reference levels valid? For example, if the reference levels have a regional resolution (varies between regions), it might mean that it is only valid and correct to use for normalising local variable values that are first aggregated to regional scale. However, sometimes the reference levels are insensitive to this and can be used to scale variables at the local (e.g. plot) scale. 
 -->  

The reference levels depend on salinity. There are reference values for all relevant levels of salinity in norwegian coastal waters. A value from a single station can be classified (given that the requirement of number and timing of observations are fulfilled.)

## 5. Uncertainties
### 5.1 General uncertainties
<!--# Describe the main reasons why you might not trust 100% the final value to represent the given ecosystem characteristic for the give ecosystem type. What aspects of this condition metric are most sensitive to subjective decitions? Is the spatial sampling sufficient? Does the choice of modeling framework affect the values? Definition of winter season (in south Norway the growth season for phytoplankton often starts in february, thus nutrient consumption may start already this month). Spatial sampling may be insufficient due to cost of sampling coastal water bodies.

### 7.1 Data from Vannmiljø  

<!--# Import and prepare the first dataset for analysis. Change the header from Dataset A to the name of the actual dataset. -->

```{r}

# read data in Vannmiljø format  

ntot_raw <-
  read_xlsx("~/shared/common/EEG/ecRxiv_nutrients/data/N-TOT vannmiljø saltvann des2021-nov2024.xlsx", guess_max = 50000) %>%
  mutate(
    year = lubridate::year(Tid_provetak))

```


### 7.2. Station metadata (ecoregion and water type)

```{r}

# . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . 
# Station metadata ----
# . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . # . 

vannlok_vannmiljø <- read_csv("~/shared/common/EEG/ecRxiv_nutrients/data/vannlokaliteter_kyst_2024.csv")
vf_vannmiljø <- read_csv("~/shared/common/EEG/ecRxiv_nutrients/data/vannforekomster_kyst_2024.csv")
class_limits_sum <- read_xlsx("~/shared/common/EEG/ecRxiv_nutrients/data/klassegrenser_TOTN_sommer.xlsx")
class_limits_win <- read_xlsx("~/shared/common/EEG/ecRxiv_nutrients/data/klassegrenser_TOTN_vinter.xlsx")

station_lookup <- ntot_raw %>% dplyr::select(Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn) %>% distinct()

stat_meta <- station_lookup %>% left_join(., vannlok_vannmiljø, by = c("Vannlokalitet_kode" = "lokkod")) %>% 
  left_join(., vf_vannmiljø, by = c("id" = "id"))

stat_meta_classlim_sum <- stat_meta %>% left_join(., class_limits_sum, by = "typ")
stat_meta_classlim_win <- stat_meta %>% left_join(., class_limits_win, by = "typ")

```

```{r take average winter values for each vannlokalitet}

ntot_mean_win <- ntot_raw %>% dplyr::mutate(year = as.numeric(str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 1)), 
                                           month = str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 2),
                                           day = substr(str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 3),1,2)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(month %in% c("12", "01", "02")) %>% 
  mutate(sesyear = case_when(month == "12" ~ year+1,
                             TRUE ~ year)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(odyp = as.numeric(Ovre_dyp), ndyp = as.numeric(Nedre_dyp)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Ovre_dyp, Nedre_dyp)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(ndyp < 11) %>%
  group_by(across(-c(odyp, ndyp, Verdi))) %>% #average in upper layer
summarise(
verdi = mean(Verdi, na.rm = T),
.groups = "drop") %>% 
  group_by(sesyear, Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn) %>% mutate(n_obs = n()) %>% #Number of observations from each water locality and year
  dplyr::filter(n_obs>= 2) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn) %>% 
  mutate(n_year = n_distinct(sesyear)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(n_year >= 2) %>% 
  group_by(across(c(Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn))) %>% 
summarise(
  verdi = mean(verdi, na.rm = T),
  .groups = "drop"
)
# 104 vannlokaliteter

ntot_mean_sum <- ntot_raw %>% dplyr::mutate(year = as.numeric(str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 1)), 
                                           month = str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 2),
                                           day = substr(str_split_i(Tid_provetak, "-", 3),1,2)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(month %in% c("06", "07", "08")) %>% 
  mutate(sesyear = case_when(month == "12" ~ year+1,
                             TRUE ~ year)) %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(odyp = as.numeric(Ovre_dyp), ndyp = as.numeric(Nedre_dyp)) %>% 
  dplyr::select(-c(Ovre_dyp, Nedre_dyp)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(ndyp < 11) %>%
  group_by(across(-c(odyp, ndyp, Verdi))) %>% #average in upper layer
summarise(
verdi = mean(Verdi, na.rm = T),
.groups = "drop") %>% 
  group_by(sesyear, Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn) %>% mutate(n_obs = n()) %>% #Number of observations from each water locality and year
  dplyr::filter(n_obs>= 2) %>% ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn) %>% 
  mutate(n_year = n_distinct(sesyear)) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(n_year >= 2) %>% 
  group_by(across(c(Vannlokalitet_kode, Vannlokalitetsnavn))) %>% 
summarise(
  verdi = mean(verdi, na.rm = T),
  .groups = "drop"
)

#138 vannlokaliteter
```

```{r join with station/vannlokalitet metadata, including class limits}

ntot_mean_win_meta <- ntot_mean_win %>% left_join(., stat_meta_classlim_win, by = c("Vannlokalitet_kode", "Vannlokalitetsnavn"))
ntot_mean_sum_meta <- ntot_mean_sum %>% left_join(., stat_meta_classlim_sum, by = c("Vannlokalitet_kode", "Vannlokalitetsnavn"))
```

The calculation of nEQR is based on 
```{r calculate_nEQR}

# calculate nEQR for each water locality  
# 
ntot_win_neqr <- ntot_mean_win_meta %>% mutate(nEQR = case_when(verdi >= X20 ~ 0.1,
                              verdi < X20 & verdi >= X40 ~ 0.3,
                              verdi < X40 & verdi >= X60 ~ 0.5,
                              verdi < X60 & verdi >=  X80 ~ 0.7,
                              verdi < X80 ~ 0.9,
                              TRUE ~ NA))  

mean(ntot_win_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
median(ntot_win_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
sd(ntot_win_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
length(!is.na(ntot_win_neqr$nEQR))

ntot_sum_neqr <- ntot_mean_sum_meta %>% mutate(nEQR = case_when(verdi >= X20 ~ 0.1,
                              verdi < X20 & verdi >= X40 ~ 0.3,
                              verdi < X40 & verdi >= X60 ~ 0.5,
                              verdi < X60 & verdi >=  X80 ~ 0.7,
                              verdi < X80 ~ 0.9,
                              TRUE ~ NA))  

mean(ntot_sum_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
median(ntot_sum_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
sd(ntot_sum_neqr$nEQR, na.rm = T)
length(!is.na(ntot_sum_neqr$nEQR))


```

As an example, we show the measured value
```{r distribution of nEQR values}

# Distribution of nEQR values
hist(ntot_sum_neqr$nEQR)

hist(ntot_win_neqr$nEQR)

```





## 10. Results

<!--# 

Repeat the final results here. Typically this is a map or table of indicator values.

This is typically where people will harvest data from, so make sure to include all relevant output here, but don't clutter this section with too much output either.

-->
The distribution of nEQR values is highly skewed both for summer and winter, with the majority of observations indicating "very good" or "good" ecological status, and a few indicating "moderate" status.

The results by ecoregion for 2022-2024 are shown below.

```{r}

ntot_sum_neqr |> 
  select(reg, nEQR) %>% 
  group_by(reg) %>% summarize(`median nEQR`= median(nEQR))|> 
  kable()  

ntot_win_neqr |> 
  select(reg, nEQR) %>% 
  group_by(reg) %>% summarize(`median nEQR`= median(nEQR))|> 
  kable()  

```
